newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU wheat aid hits double figures as prices slide.
newsitem.headline: EU wheat aid hits double figures as prices slide.

text.p: European Union (EU) grain subsidies stepped up a gear on Thursday when the EU nearly doubled the aid given for wheat exports to keep pace with falling world markets.

Grain exporters said EU officials in Brussels had awarded wheat export subsidies up to 13 Ecus per tonne for 290,000 tonnes of wheat, stretching into double figures for the first time this season and raising market competition another notch.
In a twist no-one had expected, the subsidy turned out higher than the special aid of 12 Ecus per tonne the EU offered for Africa's poorest states just a week ago.
"I'm amazed. Anyone who took the 12 Ecus has been cheated on," a European trader said.
But the London-based International Grains Council warned on Thursday prices would stay at the mercy of tight stocks despite a six percent rise in world supplies to 573.2 million tonnes.
Traders noted the setback in world prices had at last removed the political mire surrounding recent sales of French wheat to Egypt at $164 per tonne or more.

The EU, which has pledged not to undercut U.S. wheat to avoid new subsidy disputes with Washington, had refused to cover the cheapest part of the sale with refunds as long as U.S. export prices at the Gulf remained significantly higher.
One official had said covering the sale was "politically impossible" if it meant undercutting U.S. prices abroad.
But with U.S. soft red wheat now trading below $156 per tonne, the EU was able to cover those and other recent sales on Thursday with an export award valued at around $160 per tonne.
